key_insight: World models only need an explicit context encoder when the agent’s own history cannot already recover the latent context that drives environment dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This paper gives a practical test for deciding whether contextual inputs are actually useful in model-based RL, helping avoid unnecessary complexity and mismatched architecture choices.
method: Defines predictive sufficiency to measure what extra next-step prediction power the true context provides beyond agent history.
Decomposes this into history-recoverable signal, residual context-dependent signal, and finite-model deficit.
Estimates predictive headroom from ordinary trained agents without needing a reference policy.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate the criterion across environments with varying identification difficulty, showing that the same task can have either positive predictive headroom or effectively zero depending on the agent’s induced visitation distribution and prior.
watch_item: A finite learned state may only partially expose the remaining headroom, so empirical estimates can understate whether a true context encoder would still help.
paper_title: Considering Context: When World Models Need Context Encoders
